title: Exporter Contract Testkit and Sink Probe Runbook for OTLP→Tempo/Jaeger Compatibility
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, reproducible contract testkit and a production-capable sink probe that validate OpenTelemetry exporter behavior against our supported backends (Tempo and legacy Jaeger ingestion). The kit should run in CI for PRs touching exporters and in nightly/regression pipelines, and the sink probe should be deployable as a small service (k8s job or sidecar) for smoke tests in staging and optional continuous probes in Dedicated/Private customer environments.

Motivation: We repeatedly see subtle regressions where exporters change envelope shapes, timestamps, or compression semantics that only surface in production trace loss or corrupted spans. Existing ad-hoc tests are brittle and do not capture failure modes like partial attribute serialization, batching edge-cases, or transient backend errors. A formalized contract test harness + a probe will let us catch regressions early, quantify exporter health, and produce actionable telemetry for SRE/Platform.
acceptance_criteria: A golden test fixture suite (set of representative spans/traces including high-cardinality attributes, nested span trees, and delayed KV cache patterns) exists and is checked into obs-infra/test-fixtures

A contract test runner that can validate exporter outputs against Tempo/Jaeger ingest endpoints (via local mock and real backend staging) is available and runnable in CI (GitHub Actions workflow) and as a dev CLI

A sink probe service implementing: (1) synthetic span generator, (2) configurable latency/error injection, (3) verification step that asserts spans reach backend with expected attributes and traceIDs, and (4) a brief health endpoint exposing last-check-status and latency percentiles
Nightly job includes fuzz runs and at-least-one regression golden compare; failures create an automated issue with failing fixture and stack traces
Dashboard panels added to APM/Console: exporter contract pass rate, median ingest latency to Tempo, 95th percentile ingest latency, and contract test failure trend over 30d
CI gating: PRs that modify exporters or ingest shims must pass contract tests or be explicitly flagged with a rationale and reviewer approval
implementation_plan: Week 0: Prototype lightweight Tempo/Jaeger sink mock that accepts OTLP/HTTP and records received envelopes; implement golden-fixture loader

Week 1: Build contract test runner (Go) that sends fixtures through configured exporter code paths (local) and compares received spans with normalization rules; add normalization for traceid/ts ordering and attribute canonicalization
Week 2: Create sink-probe service (k8s Job + Dockerfile) with config for burst sizes, attribute fuzzing, header variants, and error injection to simulate partial writes/backpressure
Week 3: Integrate runner into GitHub Actions matrix for exporter packages and add nightly fuzz job that runs against staging Tempo; wire failures to issue-creation automation
Week 4: Dashboards and alerting: add panels to Console observability space and a derived metric for contract-test pass rate; add playbook entries to runbook
Runbook: document how SRE/Platform triages test failures, reproduces with local runner, and escalates to exporter owners
notes_and_tradeoffs: Normalization rules: we will canonicalize timestamps and traceID formatting to avoid brittle diffs; this means some checksum-level differences won't fail the contract but behaviorally significant changes (missing attributes, changed span kind) will fail
Performance: probe will intentionally not run volume-scale scenarios — the goal is correctness and common edge cases; throughput/scale benchmarking remains in a separate workload test
Operational cost: nightly fuzz runs increase staging load; limit to 1h/day and sample fixtures to keep costs predictable
Backends: prototype targets Tempo and Jaeger only; adding other vendor backends will be a follow-up (low priority)
Security: the probe will not send production data; fixtures must be synthetic and scrubbed; no PII allowed
